Koleksi skill, referensi dan aset kreatif — dipahami sebagai entitas independen, bukan dipaksa menjadi satu alur.

VERSI 1.0STATIC AUDIT21 NOVEMBER 2026
Inventaris

Seluruh file sumber tercatat satu per satu.

Anatomi isi

Struktur teks, kode, data dan metadata.

Bukti aktual

Path, nama modul, duplikasi dan topik spesifik.

Batas kepastian

Tidak mengklaim menonton atau mendengar media.

Tujuan dokumen. Menjadi peta pengetahuan repositori yang objektif dan dapat ditelusuri. Setiap file memiliki status baca dan keterkaitan sendiri.

Basis: snapshot lokal files/; tanpa menjalankan instruksi skill atau mengubah berkas sumber. Laporan pelaksanaan dan inventaris status ada di agent-log.md.

Kontrol dokumen & batas bukti

Snapshot lokal seluruh isi files/; entitas diperlakukan terpisah sampai ada bukti keterkaitan. Tidak ada satu pipeline produksi yang diasumsikan untuk seluruh koleksi.

ElemenKeterangan
Tanggal21 November 2026 · UTC
Cakupan960 file sumber dalam 144 subdirektori di bawah files/ (tidak menghitung files/ sendiri). Dua output audit tidak masuk denominator.
MetodePembacaan teks penuh, parsing JSON/kode statis, ekstraksi seluruh halaman PDF, decoding citra, metadata audio/video, pencarian rujukan lokal dan pembandingan duplikat.
StatusInventaris lengkap; analisis teks statis selesai. Pemahaman semantik media belum lengkap dan tidak diklaim selesai.
Templatefiles/agent/sample-style.html · CSS asli disalin utuh; isi blueprint contoh tidak dianggap fakta repo.
ReproduksibilitasID per file, path, ukuran, status baca, struktur isi, kutipan dan bukti hubungan disediakan di katalog.
Pemisahan penting: membaca byte ≠ menonton/mendengar; transkrip ≠ verifikasi gerak; checksum identik ≠ bukti alur kerja; satu folder ≠ dependensi. Kutipan instruksi “always/global” di skill adalah isi sumber, bukan aturan yang diterapkan pada audit.

2. Peta koleksi skill (tanpa menyatukan workflow)

Mr omi

Paket cartoon-3d-short: contoh film jembatan, style bible, laporan karakter/lighting/depth/outline/grade, implementasi Three.js + Remotion dan sintesis audio NumPy/SciPy. Hubungan dalam paket terlihat dari import dan path template. Referensi ke lokasi ~/bridge-short atau src/videos adalah target proyek contoh, bukan otomatis file yang tersedia di sini.

adilinthewildtempo

Dua tutorial monetisasi/kanal faceless, skill akuisisi klien, UGC, motion, script, production, Seedance prompts dan packaging. Client finder membatasi pengambilan kontak bisnis publik dan meminta persetujuan sebelum mengirim Gmail, maksimum 50/hari dan hanya bila diizinkan. Persetujuan render pada motion berbeda dari persetujuan email; tidak ada tindakan eksternal dijalankan.

joeysnoisygroup

Lima SKILL.md: Castkit untuk identitas karakter; Scenecraft untuk plate lingkungan; Shotcaller v2 untuk prompt Seedance/shot; Story Bible Builder untuk kanon; Voicesheet v1 untuk referensi karakter bersuara. Voicesheet menyebut Castkit dan Shotcaller secara eksplisit. Kompatibilitas output bukan berarti kelimanya wajib berantai.

kaye_creatives

Koleksi terbesar: tutorial motion, mesin reel editorial, film kolase, gaya painted-2d, CINEDANCE block library, paket JKD dan ekspor blog Notion. Empat paket tersalin di beberapa lokasi. JKD adalah subsistem tersendiri; tidak ada bukti harus dipakai untuk reel talking-head atau semua aset di folder lain.

sanjii

Cartoon Scene Builder dan dua versi ricksclips-short-style. Kedua rules.json identik tetapi SKILL.md berbeda. Varian lebih lengkap menambahkan tooling puppet, contoh rig dan layer PNG; jangan menyamakan dua paket hanya berdasarkan nama skill.

files/skill/joeysnoisygroup/All My Claude Skills for Better Prompting/skill/castkit-v1/SKILL.mdDefinisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Castkit v1 — character builder. A skill made by Joey. Builds reusable character reference images, photoreal or animated, for Nano Banana Pro and other image models. Five stations: face lock (a new character's canonical chest-up plate), additions (hair changes, piercings, tattoos, scars, expression sets, re-locks), single-image outfit builds straight onto the locked character, outfit replacement (two-reference swap), and character sheets (3-panel default with headless front, full rear and tight face panel; every panel dead-on, never a three-quarter turn unless asked; 6-panel on request). Every plate renders on a flat 18% neutral gray field, shadowless and with no cast shadow, so no lighting bakes in. Use this skill whenever the user wants to design or lock a character, build a face, turn a photoreal character animated, change hair or markings, put an outfit or garment references on a character, swap a face onto an outfit, make a character sheet, turnaround or model sheet, or any character reference still.0 rujukan path lokal teresolusi
files/skill/joeysnoisygroup/All My Claude Skills for Better Prompting/skill/scenecraft-v1/SKILL.mdDefinisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Scenecraft v1 — scene plate builder. A skill made by Joey. Writes photoreal environment plates, location plates, set and world plates, coverage angles, and people-in-scene stills for Nano Banana Pro, Seedream 5.0 Pro, and any other image model. Plans composition silently with thirds placement and a resolution-aware detail filter, then writes the prompt as confident five-paragraph cinematographer prose closed by a film-capture finish. Covers day, night exterior, lit night interior, action, performance, editorial and empty registers, full-frame atmosphere without fog, light by direction, quality and temperature, and prompt-guided edits to an existing plate. Use this skill whenever the user wants a scene plate, an environment, a location, a background, a world or set reference, an establishing still, reverse or matching angles of a place, a character placed into a scene, or a first frame for video generation, even if they never say the word plate.0 rujukan path lokal teresolusi

Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Build or check vertical Shorts in the @ricksclips3000 house style - measured style rules, camera math, and a three.js stage that renders 2D cutout characters in a sunlit 3D set to MP4.9 rujukan path lokal teresolusi
files/skill/sanjii/How to Make Viral Animated Shorts in Claude/ricksclips-short-style/SKILL.mdDefinisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: The channel skill for @ricksclips3000-style animated Shorts - flat 2D doodle characters living in a sunlit 3D world, built entirely in code. Use it whenever the user wants to make, plan, render or check a vertical Short in this style, mentions "the channel skill", or asks for any step of it - generate the main character, an emotion sheet, slice a character into layers or rig a puppet, hand-painted textures, a 3D model of a prop, a background, the voiceover or music, "build the full 3D scene in code", a stop-frame check, a numbers comparison with a reference frame, or pastes a script and asks for the video. Generates every asset through the Higgsfield connector and assembles, checks and renders the video with the bundled three.js stage.14 rujukan path lokal teresolusi
Higgsfield MCP (https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp) sering disebut sebagai layanan eksternal. Dependensi dinyatakan hanya untuk dokumen yang menyebutnya; audit ini tidak menghubungkan layanan, tidak mengeksekusi skill dan tidak menggenerasi aset. Klaim hasil bisnis di tutorial adalah klaim sumber.

3. Anatomi subsistem JKD FIGHT ENGINE

Paket v2.12.0 adalah arsip riset, registri dan sistem pengarahan adegan laga, bukan basis pengetahuan yang telah diverifikasi ulang terhadap semua film.

6. Modul/aset Standalone & hubungan yang tidak terbukti

Definisi operasional: Standalone berarti tidak ditemukan hubungan eksplisit lokal pada pemindaian ini, bukan bukti bahwa file tidak mungkin berhubungan. Parent folder, kesamaan ekstensi, nomor dan tema umum tidak digunakan sebagai hubungan. Aset yang hanya punya padanan duplikat diberi status tersendiri.

Koleksi yang tidak dipaksakan menyatu

  • Paket Mr omi, Joey, adil, JKD, reel editorial, painted-2d, kolase dan ricksclips adalah keluarga mandiri satu terhadap lainnya, kecuali rujukan spesifik yang tercatat.
  • Enam images/ dan dua styles/ adalah referensi mandiri. Tidak ada dasar menetapkan satu gaya sebagai default seluruh repositori.
  • Seluruh vo/ belum dipetakan ke video. Kemiripan judul atau perkiraan bahasa tidak cukup.
  • Video bernomor tidak otomatis bersesuaian dengan nomor judul pada PDF. Hanya salinan Nas 96 yang terbukti identik.
  • sample-style.html dipakai sebagai template dokumen ini, bukan sebagai bagian pipeline generasi media.

Daftar lengkap tanpa rujukan lokal/duplikat terdeteksi

245 file. Padanan topik PDF dikecualikan dari daftar ini dan dijelaskan terpisah; padanan tersebut bukan dependency kode.

files/skill/Mr omi/youtube.com:watch?v=OtbLL6OBNE4/github.com:mromidev:claude-animated-shorts/claude-animated-shorts-main/README.md · 2275 byte · .md

Fungsi / isi. Dokumen petunjuk instalasi/pemakaian: Claude Animated Shorts.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Claude Animated Shorts → What's inside → Install → Notes → License
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Claude Animated Shorts The free Claude skill from the video **"How to Make Viral Animated Shorts Using Claude (Full Workflow)"**. It makes 55-70 s vertical animated story shorts: 2D characters in a colourful 3D world, with ink outlines, a painted town, lens blur, gliding cameras, a march score and sound effects. Everything is rendered with three.js inside Remotion on your own PC, with no AI video generator. Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Make a ~55-70 s vertical cartoon story short in the "2D characters in a colourful 3D world" style (flat bean-head cartoon cards with ink outlines, painted 3D town/world with black ink lines, saturated sky, depth-of-field backgrounds, gliding cameras, voice narration, synthesized SFX + march-style music), rendered with three.js inside Remotion. Proven on "The Bridge That Fell for a Song" (2026-10-31). Use when the user asks for another video "like the bridge video", "like the soldiers/bridge short", "in that cartoon 3D style", a history/science story short with cartoon characters in 3D, or says "use the cartoon short skill".

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Cartoon 3D story short (three.js + Remotion) → Pipeline → Final look values (bridge after 4 verifier rounds; all in `templates/bridge/`) → Look targets (measured from the reference; see references/reports/) → Look-match loop (how the bridge look was reached; reuse for any "make it look like X" pass) → Gotchas → Readability traps the verifier caught (check every new prop/shot for these)
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Cartoon 3D story short (three.js + Remotion) Proven example: **The Bridge That Fell for a Song**. It is an original 67 s short about the 1831 Broughton bridge and 74 soldiers marching in step. - Code: `src/videos/bridge/` of your Remotion project (composition `BridgeShort`, 1080x1920, 30 fps). - Script, voice and sound: `~/bridge-short/`. - Style research: `references/`. The style reference is a channel studied privately (`references/`: STYLE_BIBLE.md, reports/*.md, frames/). - Those videos are private study material. Never upload, publish or send them. - Never copy their scripts, characters or shots. Story, characters and voice are always OUR OWN. - Never say the channel's name in a voice-over or description. User rules that apply: - No captions or labels in the video. - English only. - Voice: one steady tone. - Jokes are researched real facts. - Standard mix: music +3 dB, SFX -6 dB, voice unchanged. - Final export 2K vertical: 1440x2560, `--scale 1.3333`.
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): - Those videos are private study material.   • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): the reference channel style bible (study of latest 20 shorts, 2026-10-30) → Format → Script formula (20/20 follow it) → Picture → Camera / editing (measured) → Effects
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # the reference channel style bible (study of latest 20 shorts, 2026-10-30) Private study only. Videos: vids/ (720p, original EN audio), transcripts: tx/, per-video measurements: measure/summary.json, 30 fps contact sheets: measure/<video>_sheets/ (each sheet = 2 s, 60 frames). ## Format - Vertical 1080x1920, 30 fps, 31-78 s (median ~60 s), voice starts at frame 1-4 (no intro, no logo, no outro, no CTA). - Voice: one male narrator, fast and steady: 3.5-4.1 words/s (median 3.7), almost no pauses (word gaps >0.25 s total <1 s per video). - Loudness -14 LUFS integrated, LRA ~2.4 LU (heavily compressed). Music/SFX bed under voice only ~5-10 dB below speech. - Captions: one word (sometimes 2-3) at a time, white bold sans, thin black outline, lower-middle, hard swaps on each word. (OUR RULE: no captions unless the user asks.) ## Script formula (20/20 follow it) 1. **Hook = paradox stated as fact, sentence 1, no setup.** A person did something that sounds dumb/impossible with stakes, or "If you X, you'd Y", or "X is illegal, yet ...". ~10-16 words. 2. **Setting in 1-2 lines**, present tense, concrete details (time of day, a named everyman, numbers). 3. **Escalation, 3-6 beats**: others laugh / doubt / mock (short in-character dialogue lines), stakes climb. 1-2 exaggeration jokes per video (claim vs reality, "so slow X, and X was ..."). 4. **Mystery beat**: a question or "Wait, ...?" ( …
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): Private study only. Videos: vids/ (720p, original EN audio), transcripts: tx/, per-video measurements: measure/summary.json, | - Loudness -14 LUFS integrated, LRA ~2.4 LU (heavily compressed). Music/SFX bed under voice only ~5-10 dB below speech. | - **Hard cuts almost never**: 0-1 per video in 12/20 videos; most "cuts" detected are 4-frame flash effects.

The user wants our picture to be as close as possible in QUALITY and STYLE: colourful, high contrast, "targeted" colours, black ink outlines on the 3D world, painted textures, real shading/lighting on characters and world, deep blurred backgrounds, lively movement, better character shapes (heads not perfect circles, better body structure). Story, script, characters and voice stay OURS: derive general rules and numbers, never trace or copy his specific characters, props or shots. ## Reference material (private study only: never upload, publish or send any of it anywhere) - 20 reference shorts, 720x1280, 30 fps: `references/vids/NN_<id>.mp4` (01 = newest). - Contact sheets, each = 2 s = 60 frames: `references/measure/NN_<id>_sheets/sNN.jpg`. - Earlier summary: `references/STYLE_BIBLE.md`. Quick overview sheet: `references/refs_sheet.jpg`. - Extract frames yourself, e.g. `ffmpeg -v error -ss 12.4 -i references/vids/01_Mz72MuPgnGY.mp4 -frames:v 1 out.png` (use PNG for measurements; JPEG is fine for viewing). Drawing spec for our cast (600×1000 design units, soles at y=975) → 2.1 Builds → 2.2 Head contour (`blobPts` / `headBlob`) → 2.3 Line weights (u = 1% of W ≈ 2.36 units for adults) → 2.4 Colours → 2.5 Face library → 2.6 Body construction, front view → 2.7 Side view (`bodySide`) → 2.8 Shading layer → 2.9 Fitting the cast into the rules → 3.   • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Characters: how the reference builds its 2D cast vs. our bridge cast Private study. Reference frames, crops and side-by-sides stay inside `references/characters/`. No files under `your Remotion project` were edited and no new stills were rendered. Our numbers come from `toon.ts` (read only) and from stills already in `your Remotion project/out/bridge/test/`. Only general construction rules were taken from the reference. None of its characters (chef, cowboy, potato-heads and so on) is copied. **Short answer:** the user is right about the bodies, but the head diagnosis needs correcting. - **Heads.** The reference heads are actually *rounder* than ours. They are slightly wider than tall (H/W 0.93); ours are tall ellipses (H/W 1.17). What makes theirs look hand-drawn is that the shape is not a perfect ellipse: - a slightly pointed crown and a fuller jaw that narrows toward the chin, - about 10% left/right asymmetry and a few degrees of tilt, - a plum outline about 3 times thicker on the bottom/shadow side than at the top, - eyes and mouth shifted toward the side the character faces, - no blush and no catchlights in the eyes. - **Bodies.** Their adults are about 3.5 head-heights tall: a bean-shaped torso on long legs drawn as single thin ink strokes, with ink-dot hands. Ours are 2.7 head-heights, with limbs about 5 times too thick, skin-coloured ball hands and big oval boots. That …

  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Grade: colour and tone, reference vs ours Folder: `references/grade/`. Scripts are in `scripts/`, data in `data/`, images in `out/`. All reference material stays private and local. No stills were rendered and nothing under `your Remotion project` was edited; the stills were only read. ## 0. The gap in plain words Compared with the reference day frames, our day frames have four problems: - **Too dark in the mids and top.** - Median Y' is 0.436 against 0.571. - p99 is 0.783 against 0.967, so we have no near-whites. - **Big pure-black areas.** - Non-ink p5 is 0.026 against 0.234. - The reference has no black areas; its darks are coloured and lifted. - **Low-chroma lit surfaces.** Lit C* p50 is 23 against 34, and p90 is 37 against 55. - **No vignette.** Our corners are brighter than the centre at 1.46, against the reference's 0.86 darkening. Two more gaps: - **Black point.** Reference blacks are warm-lifted, with a black point of (35,19,20). Ours is blue-black, (2,0,13). - **Golden.** Ours is much darker (median 0.33 against 0.52) and over-saturated orange (HSV S p50 .71 against .45). Its shadows are brown (dark-zone b* +11), where the reference's are violet (b* −6). It is also missing the reference's roughly 25 % share of violet, blue, magenta and rose hues.

It was therefore set to 0. | Golden is the weaker fit. The golden look depends on hue content our golden scenes do not have. Use `amount` 0.8 for golden. | Stability: a first run with neutral-only tint targets reproduced the same day preset to within 0.01 (`data/grade_params_v1_neutral_only.json`). It made golden explode to a +71/255 magenta shadow tint, which is why the tint stage got its chroma, black-point and cap terms. Logs: `data/fit2_v2.log`. Presets: `data/grade_params.json`. | The grade is display-referred and expects tone-mapped input in 0..1, so it must come after `ToneMappingEffect(NEUTRAL)`. Bloom stays before tone mapping, as now.

  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Motion: reference vs ours (camera grammar + character animation) Units: **px = pixels at the reference size 720x1280** (multiply by 1.5 for our 1080x1920). **f** = frame at 30 fps. Reference = 20 shorts, 32,337 frames, burned-in caption band excluded from every camera measurement. Ours = `story.ts` / `cast.ts` / `toon.ts` as of 2026-10-31. Rendering was off-limits, so ours is measured **from the code with the same maths**: `ourcam.py` runs the exact `CAMS` + `run()` + `camAt()` (a private copy, executed with node) through the same per-frame similarity fit and the same statistics as the reference; `ourwalk.py` evaluates the `bodyFront` / `bodySide` formulas. ## 0. Verdict 1. **Our camera moves are 3-frame snaps; the reference glides.** Our key moves peak at a median 115 px/f (up to 488) with a 3 f attack. Reference moves are symmetric ease-in-out: ~10 f in, ~10 f out, ~23 f total, with a median peak of 14-16 px/f. The "ease-out burst" grammar in STYLE_BIBLE.md (and in the `story.ts` header comment) came from an integer phase correlation that cannot see motion below ~4 px/f. It is wrong. 2. **The reference camera is almost never dead still.** 65 % of frames move. Even in quiet frames it keeps pushing in (0.14 %/f median). There is no hand-held float at all. Impacts are 6-7 frame kicks that flip sign every frame. 3. **Characters are animated on ones.** No line boil, no squash/st …

Only acting idles, e.g. the v20 sleeper's head lolls 10-15° in 8-10 f, holds ~20 f, then returns. | standing figures frozen (good); water bob 0.03 m at 0.35 Hz (motivated, good). **Townsfolk wave at 1.4 Hz and the kid hops at 1.1 Hz without a break.** | extras too busy | | | Blinks | 3-4 f long: half, shut ×1-2 (a line), half. Gaps 0.2-2.3 s, typically 0.5-1.5 s (v19: 7 blinks in 4 s, v06: 6 in 4 s). Blinks cover expression swaps. | `blinkAt`: every 3.98 s, 4.3 f, open/shut only, not tied to swaps | 3-5x fewer, no in-between frames | | | Mouth (talking) | smooth shapes changing on ones (line, rect with teeth, open with tongue, wide); r ≈ 0.47 with the voice RMS; the mouth leads by 0-1 f (v10 officer) | no talking characters; expression mouths are static | n/a (narration only) | | - Any footstep or stomp sound timed to 2 steps/s must be re-timed to `marchPhase` 0 and 0.5.

  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Outlines (black ink lines on the 3D world): reference vs ours Work folder: `references/outlines/` (scripts, crops, sheets, results, recipe, toy test harness). Private study only. Nothing under `your Remotion project` was edited; no new stills were rendered. ## 1. The gap in one paragraph In the reference, **74 % of the geometry edges I scanned carry a black line (36 of 49)**: silhouettes against sky, depth jumps between objects, convex creases (box corners, table tops, wall tops, window frames) and contacts (object on floor). Lines are **~3 px wide at 1080p**, near-black in focus, crisp (anti-aliased only), and they **stay about the same width on screen** as objects get smaller, so the depth of field later blurs them along with the background. **In our stills, 0 of 20 scans across the same kinds of edges show a line.** The "lines" you see in our frames are the characters' own Canvas2D outlines and texture strokes. The current `ink.ts` cannot work in the current chain: the DOF in the same merged EffectPass erases it, and its Laplacian of 1/z cannot see creases at all (see section 4). ## 2. Measurements Method: perpendicular luma scans (averaged over 5 px across the scan, 0.25 px steps) through single edges. `EW` = equivalent full-ink width (area of the dip / (background - ink luma 12)), which does not depend on blur. A line counts as "present" if it is at least 35 % darker tha …

  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Textures: reference surface painting vs ours, and how to paint ours procedurally Topic folder: `references/textures/` (scripts, crops, data, side-by-sides, prototype). Private study only. Nothing here was uploaded, and nothing under `your Remotion project` was edited or rendered. ## 0. Bottom line The reference paints every surface as a few flat colour fields. Painted lines (board gaps, mortar, tile joints) are thin, about 3-5 px at 1080p. Sun and shade sit in a narrow, bright, saturated range, and only big shapes vary in tone. Our surfaces miss in five ways: 1. **Too dark.** Our deck renders at L* 50, the reference at L* 72-80. Iron and side beams render at L* 3-7, where the reference never goes below L* 19. 2. **Too dull.** Our sky has C* 22-29 where the reference has 40-89. Our golden sky is a grey-mauve at C* 16-19. 3. **Lines too heavy and blurry.** Our gaps and mortar are 1.5-2.5x wider, and their 10-90 % edge ramps are 4-6 px. 4. **Water texture wrong.** Ripple marks are spread evenly at 4-12 % area and form vertical streaks, and there is no depth gradient. 5. **Flat clouds.** Ours are one flat tone. The reference uses three tones with a lavender underside. Everything below is measured. The recipe in section 5 has been type-checked, and its water and deck output was measured in a CPU preview against the reference numbers (section 5.6). ## 1. Method - **Reference:** 91 …

Fungsi / isi. Dokumen referensi/tutorial: "The Bridge That Fell for a Song" — original script v1 (2026-10-30).

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): "The Bridge That Fell for a Song" — original script v1 (2026-10-30)
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # "The Bridge That Fell for a Song" — original script v1 (2026-10-30) Format: the reference-Clips-style short (~55 s, ~3.7 words/s), the voice, our own characters + story. Facts: Broughton Suspension Bridge, Salford, 12 April 1831; 74 men of the 60th Rifle Corps marching four abreast; felt the bridge vibrate in time with their steps, found it amusing, some whistled a marching tune and stepped to it; a badly forged single bolt in a stay-chain snapped; one end fell 16-18 ft into the River Irwell, about 2 ft deep there; nobody killed, 20 injured; British Army then ordered troops to "break step" on bridges. (Wikipedia, Broughton Suspension Bridge) Seventy-four soldiers knocked down an iron bridge just by walking across it. It's 1831, and the brand new bridge over the river is the pride of the whole town. The men are marching home four across, every boot hitting the planks at the exact same moment. Halfway over, the bridge starts bouncing under their feet. A normal person would slow down, but these guys think it's hilarious. Somebody starts whistling a marching tune, and the whole column stomps along to it, a little harder every step. The bounce gets bigger, the chains start groaning, and nobody wants to be the one who breaks step. Then a single bolt snaps, and the whole end of the bridge drops into the river. Luckily, the river was only two feet deep. Unluckily, the river was only …
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): Luckily, the river was only two feet deep. | Unluckily, the river was only two feet deep. | Nobody died, but the army made a rule: never cross a bridge in step.
  • Cakupan pembacaan: 22 baris; 1847 karakter. Frontmatter: tidak ada.

Voice = `voice/voice.wav`, gain only (no EQ, no compression, no pitch). ## Files | file | content | | `mix.wav` | final mix, 48 kHz, stereo, 24-bit, 3,240,000 samples = 67.500 s | | `stem_voice.wav` / `stem_music.wav` / `stem_sfx.wav` | stems at mix gain (they sum to the mix before the master limiter) | ## Master loudness (own BS.1770-4 meter) - Integrated **-15.0 LUFS**, true peak **-1.2 dBTP**, LRA 2.6 LU, max momentary -9.0 LUFS, max short-term -12.5 LUFS - Stems: voice -15.4 LUFS, music -25.8 LUFS, sfx -29.1 LUFS (voice gain +1.20 dB, same gain on every stem) - Master limiter (4x oversampled look-ahead, ceiling -1.2 dBTP): max gain reduction 1.45 dB, active (>0.1 dB) on 3.53 % of samples, >0.5 dB on 0.63 % ffmpeg ebur128 cross-check: Summary: Integrated loudness: I: -15.0 LUFS Threshold: -25.0 LUFS
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): Voice = `voice/voice.wav`, gain only (no EQ, no compression, no pitch). | Rides (music only, dB): 3.65-4.30 s -3.0, 26.95-27.36 s -2.0, 32.20-32.77 s -4.0, 61.25-61.98 s -3.0 - so quiet sentence-final words stay on top and the band blooms in the gaps after them. The hook's last two footfalls (3.5, 4.0) are also 3 dB lower in the SFX for '...walking across it.' | | 59.79 | 1794 | brass stab Bb + timpani on hammer blow 1 ('rule'), F on blow 2 ('Never'), Bb + cymbal on blow 3 ('step') |

  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: Final mix of "The Bridge That Fell for a Song": the voice (gain only) + original march score (ducked under speech, per-section level automation relative to the voice) + synthesized SFX stem. Head half width ~118 units -> .2 of the card, torso ~89 -> .15. if NUM_DIR_LIGHTS > 0

Fungsi / isi. Post-processing color grade; LUT/kurva dan pilihan grade sepanjang cerita.

  • Struktur: 179 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: monoTangents, GradeEffect, gradeFor, tintRGB, KX, GradeParams, GRADE_DAY, GRADE_GOLDEN, GRADE_DAY2, GRADE_GOLDEN2, GRADES, GRADE_STRENGTH.

The presets were fitted to the OLD unlit stills: after the WORLD lighting lands they will over-correct; re-fit (grade.md 5.C) or lower GRADE_STRENGTH. Each Inner (crossfade layer) grades with its own shot's light, so the DOM crossfade at XFADE frames (shots 10->11, 13->14) cross-fades the presets as well. GradeEffect: the fitted reference-style colour grade as a postprocessing 6.37 Effect. Put it LAST in the EffectComposer, after ToneMappingEffect. It works on display-referred values: the input (linear, already tone-mapped to 0..1) is encoded to sRGB, graded exactly like scripts/grade.py (validated on our stills), and decoded back to linear for the composer's output encoding. 1. RGB tone curve: monotone cubic Hermite through 7 knots at x = 0, .1, .25, .5, .75, .9, 1 2. saturation around luma Y' (Rec.709 weights on the encoded values), separately for shadows / mids / highlights 3. 3-way tint (split tone): zero-luma RGB offsets in shadows, mids, highlights 4. vignette: x (1 - k * smoothstep(r0, 1, r)), r = elliptical radius, corners = 1 `amount` blends the whole grade (0 = bypass) so it can be dialled back once lighting/albedo work brightens the render.

Fungsi / isi. Pass kontur tinta untuk dunia 3D; lebar garis berskala terhadap resolusi dan fallback tanpa ink.

  • Struktur: 393 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: InkPass, noInkFallback, NOINK, InkOptions.
  • Import/dependensi tertulis: import * as THREE from "three"; | import { Pass } from "postprocessing";
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: Ink outlines for the 3D world, matched to the reference measurements (references/reports/outlines.md recipe, post-agent changes: widths scale with the output height (pxScale = height / 1920, so 5.1 px at 1080x1920 is 6.8 px at 1440x2560), RMAX 9 for headroom at 1440, fog-tinted ink (scene.fog, x0.3), `noInkFallback` below. Round 2: widths x1.5 (5.1 -> 3.3 px from 6 to 90 m), pure near-black #030303, far opacity 0.95, depth jumps from 1 %. How it works 1. Re-render the WORLD ONLY (camera layer 0) into a non-MSAA target: view-space normal (rgb), coverage (a) and a depth texture. Character billboards, effect cards, sky, clouds and smoke live on layer NOINK, so they never get rectangle outlines and never cut holes into the world's lines. 2. Edge mask (full resolution), pixel steps 1..6 along x, y and both diagonals: depth - signed 2nd difference of 1/z (exactly 0 on any plane, so no grazing-angle false lines) -> only the NEAR side of a depth jump is inked, as a band `width` px wide (silhouettes vs sky, object vs object, thin ropes become solid lines like the reference); crease - normal angle > ~50 deg to a neighbour at the same depth, two-sided band ~0.64*width px wide, concave folds (object meets ground, inner corners) at 0.7 strength; coverage is continuous in the width (no width popping when the camera moves), width shrinks a little with distance (3.4 px at 6 m -> 2.2 px at 90 m, log-distance), opacity to 0.75, fades out by 450 m; no ink where the main depth buffer has something nearer than the world (characters / cards in front). 3. Composite: 3x3 tent-filtered mask (anti-aliasing), near-black ink blended in display gamma (like Canvas2D), written back into the input buffe …
  • Operasi I/O/CLI terpilih: renderer.render(scene, cam); | renderer.render(this.fsScene, this.fsCam); | renderer.render(this.fsScene, this.fsCam); | renderer.render(this.fsScene, this.fsCam);

files/skill/Mr omi/youtube.com:watch?v=OtbLL6OBNE4/github.com:mromidev:claude-animated-shorts/claude-animated-shorts-main/templates/bridge/lensblur.ts · 7962 byte · .ts

Fungsi / isi. Efek depth of field/lens blur dan grain; perhitungan circle of confusion dari kedalaman dan fokus.

  • Struktur: 139 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: LensBlurEffect, LensBlur, GrainEffect.
  • Import/dependensi tertulis: import { Effect, EffectAttribute, BlendFunction } from "postprocessing"; | import { Uniform } from "three";
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: Thin-lens depth of field for the reference's soft backgrounds (reports/depth.md 6.1), as two deterministic gather passes. CoC radius (px at 1080x1920) = cInf * |1 - focus / depth|, x nearScale in front of the focus plane, clamped to maxCoC. Every pixel size is multiplied in the shader by (output height / 1920), so the picture is the same at 540, 1080 and 1440 widths. pre : 16-tap gather over 0.29 x the CoC. It fills the gaps between the main taps, so the composite kernel is a smooth disc (1024 effective taps) instead of 64 visible copies of every edge. main : 64-tap Vogel disc over 0.96 x the CoC (pre + main together = a disc of sigma CoC/2), plus a 32-tap near field gather that lets a blurred foreground spread over sharper pixels behind it. Occlusion rules (no halos, no dark rims): a sample counts only if its own CoC reaches this pixel, a farther sample may never spread wider than this pixel's own CoC (sharp subjects keep clean silhouettes), and the result is renormalised by the accepted weights. Fixed sample pattern, no per-pixel noise: no grain, no frame-to-frame flicker. Both passes are CONVOLUTION effects, so R3F's <EffectComposer> gives each its own EffectPass. define GOLDEN 2.39996323

Fungsi / isi. Preset pencahayaan menurut waktu; matahari relatif kamera dibekukan per shot.

  • Struktur: 63 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: LightPreset, LIGHTS, WorldLook, LOOK.
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: Light presets per time of day. The sun is CAMERA-RELATIVE and frozen per shot (world.ts update()): az = degrees from the shot camera's forward axis (0 = sun straight ahead = backlight, +90 = screen right, 180 = behind camera), el = elevation. lit/shade/lift are LINEAR RGB multipliers for shade.ts (may exceed 1). Field names follow lighting.md 9.1 exactly (the CHAR and POST agents read them); values are tuned on renders.

files/skill/Mr omi/youtube.com:watch?v=OtbLL6OBNE4/github.com:mromidev:claude-animated-shorts/claude-animated-shorts-main/templates/bridge/shade.ts · 5385 byte · .ts

Fungsi / isi. Pencahayaan toon dua tingkat berdasarkan albedo, warna terang/bayang dan shadow map.

  • Struktur: 77 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: twoTone, TONE, CHAR, LFB, untone.
  • Import/dependensi tertulis: import * as THREE from "three";
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: Stylised two-tone lighting for every world material (lighting.md 9.2, world part): albedo x mix(shadeCol, litCol, sunTerm), sunTerm = real shadow-map visibility x a soft N.L terminator. The sun visibility is captured inside three's own light loop (LFB), so nothing is computed twice. Character cards (cardShade) live in the CHAR agent's file and can import LFB / CHAR from here; world.ts sets every uniform below once per frame from LIGHTS. character-card uniforms (lighting.md 9.2 cardShade); world.ts keeps them in sync with LIGHTS for cardshade.ts */ directional light 0 = the sun = the only shadow caster (three sorts shadow-casting lights first). Only the UNROLLED index 0 compiles the shadow block, so sunVis is written once.

Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Find businesses that are likely to pay for AI content, write a personal message for each one and send it from the user's Gmail. Use whenever the user wants to find clients, build a prospect list, find leads for UGC videos, product photos, motion ads, real-estate visuals, or websites, or asks "who can I sell this to?" Searches the user's niche, spots businesses whose listings show the exact problem the user's service fixes, collects only contacts the business itself has officially published (no personal data, no research into the people behind a business), drafts a personal message for each one and, once the user approves, sends them through the Gmail connector — no more than 50 a day, and only where cold business email is allowed.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Higgsfield Client Finder → Step 1 — Brief → Step 2 — Find well-matched leads → Step 3 — Draft a personal message for each lead → Step 4 — Approve and send through Gmail → Responsible use (always follow)
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Higgsfield Client Finder You help the user go from "who do I even write to?" to a short list of well-matched businesses, each with a reason to reach out and a personal message, sent from the user's own Gmail. Three principles run through everything: 1. **Right fit over big numbers.** Ten businesses with a real, visible problem beat a hundred random ones. 2. **Only official public business contacts.** Use only contact details a business has chosen to publish for business enquiries. Research the business, never the people behind it. 3. **The user approves, Gmail sends.** Nothing goes out until the user has seen the list and the messages and said yes. Then send each message from the user's Gmail, no more than 50 a day. --- ## Step 1 — Brief Ask in one short message: 1. **What are you selling?** UGC videos / product photos / motion ads / real-estate visuals (photo upgrades, video tours) / websites / a package. 2. **Target niche and place:** for example, kitchenware sellers on online marketplaces, independent clothing brands with their own online stores, short-term rental hosts and small hotels in a specific city, local dentists or gyms without a modern website. The country matters: it decides whether a cold email is allowed at all (see Step 4). 3. **How many leads:** 10, 25, or 50. Fifty is the daily sending maximum (see Step 4). 4. **Portfolio:** a link or 2–3 sample pieces the …

Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Castkit v1 — character builder. A skill made by Joey. Builds reusable character reference images, photoreal or animated, for Nano Banana Pro and other image models. Five stations: face lock (a new character's canonical chest-up plate), additions (hair changes, piercings, tattoos, scars, expression sets, re-locks), single-image outfit builds straight onto the locked character, outfit replacement (two-reference swap), and character sheets (3-panel default with headless front, full rear and tight face panel; every panel dead-on, never a three-quarter turn unless asked; 6-panel on request). Every plate renders on a flat 18% neutral gray field, shadowless and with no cast shadow, so no lighting bakes in. Use this skill whenever the user wants to design or lock a character, build a face, turn a photoreal character animated, change hair or markings, put an outfit or garment references on a character, swap a face onto an outfit, make a character sheet, turnaround or model sheet, or any character reference still.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Castkit v1 — Character & Outfit Builder → The five stations → STEP ZERO — THE RENDER FORK → The animated style lock → CORE PRINCIPLES → Two axes — keep them separate → The flattering ceiling (every face, both styles) → Prompt economy → THE FLAT GRAY FIELD (LOCKED DEFAULT) → PHOTOREAL FLAT CLOSE — verbatim on every photoreal plate → ANIMATED FLAT CLOSE — verbatim on every animated plate, style lock first → READING REFERENCES → THE PRE-PROMPT CHECK → STATION 0 — FACE LOCK → Stage 1 — The text spec → Stage 2 — The tool fork → Step 0.1 — Soul Cinema test (optional, photoreal only) → Step 0.2 — The canonical lock → STATION 1 — ADDITIONS → STATION 2 — OUTFIT BUILD (SINGLE IMAGE) → Step 1 — The outfit proposal (text only) → Step 2 — Build it directly on the character → Repair only — the invisible mannequin plate → STATION 3 — OUTFIT REPLACEMENT → STATION 4 — CHARACTER SHEETS → 3-panel layout → Orientation lock — dead-on always → The headless cut — chosen by the neckline → Variant A — ghost mannequin → Variant B — clean neck cut → 3-panel prompt → Extra panels — the 6-panel (explicit request only) → Rules for every sheet → UNIVERSAL RULES → DELIVERY → PRE-DELIVERY PASS → REPAIR PASS

Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Motiondojo v1 — motion transfer prompt director for Higgsfield Genjutsu. A skill made by Joey. Writes lean Genjutsu prompts that take the movement from an attached motion transfer video and put it on new characters in a new world, with true gravity and bodyweight on every move. Three forms: body copy (characters match the exact motion and the camera matches the video), camera copy (only the video's camera path carries onto a new scene), and body copy with a new camera (exact motion, with a rebuilt handheld camera that moves naturally all around it). Opens every prompt with a hard mouth lock: characters speak only the exact words spoken in the motion video, and mouths stay closed when there is no speech. Covers role assignment, individuality, population locks, and surface-aware physics. Use this skill whenever the user mentions Genjutsu, motion transfer, copying choreography, dance or camera movement from a reference video, or putting characters into someone else's moves.

Writes photoreal environment plates, location plates, set and world plates, coverage angles, and people-in-scene stills for Nano Banana Pro, Seedream 5.0 Pro, and any other image model. Plans composition silently with thirds placement and a resolution-aware detail filter, then writes the prompt as confident five-paragraph cinematographer prose closed by a film-capture finish. Then move on. The output is one character section in the format defined in `character-section-format.md`. --- ## 1. Function Start here, not with looks. Ask: **"What role does this character play in the story? Not their job — their *function*. What do they represent? What are they the emotional/narrative anchor for?"** Look for a role tag — one to three words. *The Heart. The Watcher. The Chaos. The Grounding.* This becomes the italicized tag after the character name in the header. Push if they give something generic. "The leader" is a job. "The one who feels most for the humans they're saving" is a function. --- ## 2. Visual lock Cover in this order: - **Hair.** Color (specific — "cool ash platinum" not "blonde"), length, cut, permanent features (always bangs, always center part, wispy temple pieces) - **Skin.** Tone with specifier ("warm fair," "cool fair," "olive medium," "warm deep") + finish (dewy, matte, freckled, natural). Ask what the wrong drift would be — that becomes the never-clause. - **Face structure.** Jaw, cheekbones, chin, nose, lips — one adjective each. Doll-coded, sharp-sculpted, soft, angular, refined. Push for a committed shape. - **Eyes.** Shape, size, color, any lift at the outer corner

One short paragraph or a few bullets.] **Present-tense psychology:** [Where they are RIGHT NOW as the story begins. What they're carrying. What they don't yet know. What they're about to face.] **Speech:** "[prompt-ready dialogue descriptor — register, texture, cadence, vocabulary, volume]" **Movement:** "[prompt-ready movement descriptor — gesture quality, combat posture if relevant, tics, gait]" **Stillness:** "[prompt-ready stillness descriptor — what they do at rest, hands, weight, expression, breath]" **Suno (if music scope):** "[prompt-ready singing voice descriptor — register, timbre, style, signature move]" [Optional bold sub-beats for specific narrative threads — e.g., a hidden relationship, a secret, a recurring pattern. Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Voicesheet v1 — walks users through building a speaking video character reference for Seedance: language pangram, emotion tags, ElevenLabs voice clip, black-frame video, two-panel Shotcaller prompt.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Voicesheet v1 — Speaking Character Reference Builder → HOW TO RUN THIS SKILL → STAGE 1 — LANGUAGE AND PANGRAM → Phonetic, not written → What a good pangram needs → Stock pangrams → Any other language (Dutch, Spanish, Japanese, and so on) → STAGE 2 — PERSONALITY AND TAGS → Tag the pangram → Example: the same Korean pangram, three characters → Voice design description → STAGE 3 — THE VOICE CLIP → STAGE 4 — THE VOICE VIDEO → STAGE 5 — THE CHARACTER SHEET → STAGE 6 — CHARACTER INTAKE → STAGE 7 — THE REFERENCE PROMPT (SHOTCALLER) → Attach order → Timing → The head turn → Template → After it renders → STAGE 8 — PROP SCALE REFERENCE (OPTIONAL) → TROUBLESHOOTING
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Voicesheet v1 — Speaking Character Reference Builder A skill made by Joey. It walks a user from nothing to a finished **video character reference**: one short Seedance 2.5 clip that locks a character's face, voice, outfit and way of performing dialogue, so every later generation knows how they look, sound and move. The finished reference is a two-panel clip on a flat gray field: - **Right panel:** one unbroken close-up of the face, lip-syncing a phonetic pangram in the character's own voice. The head turns naturally through the emotional range, so the model learns the bone structure from several angles and how this person emotes. - **Left panel:** a montage of full-body turns plus tight inserts of the outfit details. Optionally, a second **prop scale reference** clip shows the character holding an item (a weapon, a bag, a phone) so later generations know its size against their body. This skill runs the process. It calls on **Castkit** for character sheets and **Shotcaller** for the Seedance prompt; load those skills when you reach their steps. --- ## HOW TO RUN THIS SKILL Work through the stages in order. Each stage ends with something the user has in hand before the next one starts. Ask only what the stage needs, one short question at a time, and let the user skip anything they already have (an existing voice clip, an existing sheet). | Stage | The user ends up with | | 1. L …
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): Work through the stages in order. Each stage ends with something the user has in hand before the next one starts. Ask only what the stage needs, one short question at a time, and let the user skip anything they already have (an existing voice clip, an existing sheet). | A written pangram uses every letter. A **phonetic** pangram makes every *sound*. They are not the same, and for a voice model the sounds are what matter. Sound changes in connected speech can hide a letter's sound entirely: in Korean, 않다 is pronounced [안타], so its ㄷ is never heard as a plain ㄷ. Always check what is actually pronounced. | - Every consonant and vowel of the language, including the ones that only show up in speech (aspiration, tense consonants, final consonants, diphthongs, nasals, sound changes at word boundaries). | Once a pangram is chosen, its text is locked for every character in that language. Only the tags change per character. | - **Never change the pangram text.** Only add tags. | A Korean woman in her twenties with a cool, clean, smooth mid-register voice. Measured, controlled volume that never rises in anger, surgical precise diction, sentences cut short and exact, long deliberate pauses before key words. Dry and composed, with a faint, private amusement underneath. Native Seoul Korean pronunciation, crisp consonants, recorded close in a quiet room.

SKILL.md

files/skill/kaye_creatives/Claude Motion/talking-head-reels/SKILL.md · 7488 byte · .md

Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Turn a talking-head recording into a finished vertical 9:16 Instagram Reel / TikTok / YouTube Short in a bold editorial style - tightened pauses, kinetic Anton + Didot typography, a red / white / black-and-white palette, B-roll inserts that illustrate exactly what is being said, split screens with the speaker, camera-move transitions, film grain, voice mastered to -14 LUFS. Everything is rendered by code (Python + ffmpeg/libass) - no After Effects or other editing app needed; footage can be generated with Higgsfield (Seedance). Use this skill whenever someone wants to edit, cut, animate or "make a reel" out of a video of a person speaking to camera, add motion text or B-roll to a speaking video, or match the style of an existing reel made with it - even if they never say "EDL", "render" or "talking head".

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Talking-head reels → Requirements → What you deliver → Step 0 - setup and intake → Step 1 - prepare and analyse (scripted) → Step 2 - plan the edit (your judgement) → Step 3 - footage → Step 4 - EDL and validation → Step 5 - stills, then the render → Step 6 - revision rounds (how the user wants to work) → Other tools → Ground rules
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Talking-head reels You turn one recording of a person talking to camera into a finished vertical reel (MP4). The look is editorial and fast: the speaker is the spine of the video, and every 2-4 seconds the frame changes - a punch-in, a big word, a B-roll insert, a split screen - always driven by what is being said at that moment. The mechanics are scripted: cutting pauses, mastering the voice, mattes, and a renderer that draws every frame straight from an edit decision list (EDL). Your job is the editorial part: understanding the talk, deciding what each beat should look like, finding or generating footage that fits, writing the EDL, checking stills, and running the revision rounds with the user. ## Requirements macOS, Python 3.9+ with numpy and faster-whisper, ffmpeg with libass (Homebrew ffmpeg or imageio-ffmpeg). Optional - Xcode command line tools (Apple Vision mattes) and a Higgsfield connection (generated B-roll). ## What you deliver - `PROJECT/render/<name>_vN.mp4` - 1080x1920, H.264, AAC 320 kbps, voice at about -14 LUFS. - `PROJECT/edl.json` (and `edl_vN.json` copies per round) - the whole edit as data; re-rendering it always gives the same video.
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): changes - a punch-in, a big word, a B-roll insert, a split screen - always driven by what is being | always gives the same video. | `numpy faster-whisper imageio-ffmpeg` is the easy route. The ffmpeg must include libass (all text | Then make sure you know (ask only for what is missing - one short message): | python3 scripts/presenter_mattes.py DIR # needs swiftc; skip only if unavailable | generated clips or inserts, use them - do not regenerate what exists.

Fungsi / isi. Dokumen referensi/tutorial: B-roll - finding, generating and preparing footage.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): B-roll - finding, generating and preparing footage → Contents → 1. What good B-roll looks like here → 2. Where it may come from → 3.   • Cuplikan isi sumber: # B-roll - finding, generating and preparing footage ## Contents 1. What good B-roll looks like here 2. Where it may come from (and rights) 3. Generating clips with Seedance via Higgsfield 4. Prompt template for generated shots 5. Preparing clips: in-points, focus, mattes 6. Swapping clips later ## 1. What good B-roll looks like here - It shows exactly the thing being said, recognisable in half a second. - It moves: a camera move, a gesture, a crowd surging, a light pulsing. 2-5 s of usable motion. - It survives black-and-white: strong shapes and contrast, a clear subject. - It crops to 9:16 (or to the top half, 1080x960, for split layouts): the subject must sit where the crop lands. Wide footage is fine - set `fx` to the subject's horizontal position. - Cinematic beats generic: a lit close-up of hands on a keyboard beats a stock "office" wide shot. - Interface footage (screen recordings, UI mock-ups) works well for tech topics.
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): - It crops to 9:16 (or to the top half, 1080x960, for split layouts): the subject must sit where | Do not download or use clips from films, series, ads or other people's social posts unless the | reference clip with new people/wardrobe while keeping camera and motion. Only for footage the | the upload fails), then `media_confirm`. References must be 2-30 s long; slow a shorter clip down | character. Do not try to get around it - write an original shot from words instead (t2v), with | people and designs that do not resemble any real actor or famous character.

Fungsi / isi. Dokumen referensi/tutorial: Planning the edit - from a talk to beats.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Planning the edit - from a talk to beats → 1. Read the talk as a story → 2. Split into beats → 3. Choose the words → 4. Pick footage per beat → 5. Presenter framing plan → 6. Worked example (first 25 s of a real reel about an AI experiment) → 7. Show the plan
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Planning the edit - from a talk to beats The scripts handle the mechanics. What makes the reel work is the plan: which words become big type, which sentences get footage, where the speaker's face is the best picture. Plan on the program timeline (`analysis/program_words.json`), after the pauses are cut. ## 1. Read the talk as a story Mark four parts: - **Hook** (first 2-6 s): the promise or the provocation. It decides whether people keep watching. - **Setup**: who/what/where, the rules of the situation. - **Escalation**: the surprising turns - each turn deserves its own visual idea. - **Payoff + call to action** (last 3-6 s): the conclusion and the ask. ## 2. Split into beats A beat is one thought, usually 1.5-4 s, ending at a natural pause or a full stop. For every beat decide one primary visual: | the words are about... | show | | the speaker's opinion, emotion, a question to the viewer | presenter (wide/tight) + big word in front or a subtitle | | a concrete thing, place, event, character | B-roll insert (`full`) |
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): Alternate: never two identical treatments in a row if the third beat can be different. | 140 white, two lines) - CTA always in front of the presenter, never over B-roll.

  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # EDL schema (edl.json) The EDL is the single source of truth: the renderer draws every frame from it. All times are **program seconds** (after the pauses are cut). All coordinates are pixels in the 1080x1920 frame, origin top-left, and refer to the centre of the item (for text: the centre of the visible letters). Relative paths resolve against the project folder. A complete example: `assets/examples/example_edl.json`. The `//` comments below are explanations only - real JSON files cannot contain comments. ## Contents 1. Top level 2. presenter 3. inserts (common fields, clip objects, kinds) 4. text 5. Swapping clips 6. Tips ## 1. Top level {
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): The `//` comments below are explanations only - real JSON files cannot contain comments. | | `t0`, `t1` | program seconds; inserts must not overlap; back-to-back inserts share the boundary exactly | | A clip shorter than the time it must cover is slowed down automatically (up to 4x); prefer clips | | `solid` | `bg` colour, optional `bgclip` | a clean background for text-only beats (counters) | | "behind": false, // true = behind the presenter's head (needs head matte; only if still readable) | "keep_t1": false, // true = stop exactly at t1 (do not extend to the end of the shot)

Troubleshooting ## 1. Pipeline No editing application is involved. Three scripts turn `edl.json` into the MP4: | script | job | | `reel_plan.py` | resolves the EDL once: media sizes, presenter pieces (pauses removed, fixed framing), punch-in keys around inserts, insert timing (adjacent inserts, transition entries, split blocks), subtitle word times, the text rules (hold to end of shot, width limit) | | `render_reel.py` | composites every frame with numpy (presenter, inserts, transitions, flashes, look layers), runs several worker processes on separate frame ranges, encodes H.264 and adds the program audio | | `textass.py` | writes the kinetic type as per-frame libass subtitle events (one per text per frame, with per-letter tags) and renders them through ffmpeg's `ass` filter as transparent layers | `fontmetrics.py` reads font files so sizes match design-tool sizes (see section 4). ## 2. Commands
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): check and the full video only when the stills pass. | | empty or black edges in a still | a clip too small for its move: raise its `zoom`, check `fx`; inserts that follow each other must share the exact boundary time | | | render seems stuck | it prints when it starts; a 75 s reel takes minutes. Run it in the background and wait; do not start a second render of the same EDL at the same time |

""" import os import shutil import subprocess import sys HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) CACHE = os.path.expanduser('~/Library/Caches/talking-head-reels/bin') TOOLS = ('person_track', 'subject_mask', 'largest_subject_mask') def tool(name): if name not in TOOLS: raise ValueError(name) src = os.path.join(HERE, 'vision', name + '.swift') exe = os.path.join(CACHE, name) if os.path.exists(exe) and os.path.getmtime(exe) >= os.path.getmtime(src): return exe swiftc = shutil.which('swiftc') if not swiftc: sys.exit('ERROR: swiftc not found - install the Xcode command line tools: xcode-select --install') os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True) print('compiling %s ...' % name, flush=True) res = subprocess.run([swiftc, '-O', src, '-o', exe], capture_output=True, text=True) if res.returncode != 0: sys.exit('ERROR: could not compile %s:\n%s' % (name, res.stderr[-2000:])) return exe def upright_proxy(ffmpeg, src, dst, w, h, fps): """ffmpeg applies the rotation flag of phone videos; Vision then sees the picture the way players show it.""" subprocess.run([ffmpeg, '-v', 'error', '-y', '-i', src, '-an', '-vf', 'scale=%d:%d:flags=bicubic,fps=%s' % (w, h, fps), '-c:v', 'prores_ks', '-profile:v', '0', dst], check=True) return dst

Here is my voiceover: /path/to/my_voiceover.wav Turn it into the finished reel: cut out all pauses and breaths, write the visual story from what I say, generate every picture in Higgsfield (a host lip-synced to my voice on an old TV, the characters, the locations, the story clips, the music), and build it in After Effects. Every generated clip goes in a floating rounded glass frame with a thin glowing border and a smooth push-in. When I list points, put a moving perspective grid behind them and flip each keyword's colour right as I say it. The main captions are big and spread across the frame, and the glass cards land exactly on the cut. Check it, fix what looks off, and render the final 1080p MP4. Optional additions to the same message: - `Script: <paste the text>`: names and spelling in the captions will then match the script. - `Make the host look like me: /path/to/my_photo.jpg` - `Look: colour, modern tech documentary`. The default is a black-and-white 1950s archival documentary. - `Accent colour: #FF3B30` Claude asks twice along the way:

Work through the Higgsfield tools: - `generate_image`, `generate_video` and `generate_audio`, or their `_batch` versions for several at once; - `media_upload` + `media_confirm` for local files (the faceboxed sheets and the host audio chunks); - `jobs_wait` until the jobs finish; - download the results into `<proj>/assets/`. Before you start: - check the balance; - add up the cost of the whole list and ask the user **once**; - make a project with folders 01 Characters / 02 Locations / 03 Video / 04 Audio when the tools support it. Test one item of each kind first (one sheet, one clip). Look at it, then batch the rest. ## Shared style line (put it at the start of every image and video prompt; adapt the era and place to the script) > Black-and-white 16mm archival documentary footage from a 1950s social-experiment film: heavy natural film grain, slight gate > weave, soft contrast, faint scratches and dust, real practical light, observational camera. For a modern or colour subject, swap in a matching documentary look. Keep it one look for the whole reel. People:
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): - The screen must be a flat, uniform chroma green, so that `reel.py screen` and the AE key find it. | > texture, no beauty filter. Soft diffused studio lighting, unretouched photography, sharp focus. Single subject only, exactly | > Realistic, grounded, no blood. Only these people. No text, no logos, no music. | - `generate_audio` must be true: `reel.py align` reads the clip's own sound to sync the lips. | ## 8. Logos (only for names that are spoken)

Fungsi / isi. Jembatan zsh untuk mengirim ExtendScript ke After Effects aktif dan menunggu hasil; lock/log dan kode keluar membedakan error, timeout, busy atau script tidak mulai.

  • Struktur: 79 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: __w.
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: !/bin/zsh ae_run.sh <script.jsx> [timeoutSec=900] Sends one ExtendScript file to the running After Effects and waits for it. The only way this skill talks to AE. Inside the script use aeLog("text") to report (DoScript return values are useless). Printed here when AE finishes. Env: AE_APP (app name, default: newest "Adobe After Effects 20xx" in /Applications), AE_LOCK_ROOT (lock + logs). Exit: 0 ok · 3 script threw (ERROR line) · 4 AE still running it after the timeout (do NOT resend; wait, then check the log) 5 lock busy · 6 AE never started it (not running / modal dialog open) — safe to resend after fixing that. ---------- lock (one script at a time per Mac); a lock older than 30 min or of a dead process is taken over

Fungsi / isi. Pipeline gambar reel: komposit kanvas lalu pass WebGL bloom, halation, grade, gate weave, grain, debu/goresan dan flash; frame ditentukan indeks waktu.

  • Struktur: 315 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: Picture.
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: A_v15 picture pipeline (A_v03 base, A_v14 film look, A_v15 rewrite of grain / bloom / B&W / archive age). 1. compose(): the shot runtime draws the current shot into a 2D "comp" canvas. 2. post(): WebGL passes over the comp. Everything is a pure function of the frame index — scrubbing is exact. a) bright-pass + 4× downsample b) separable Gaussian (H, V) at quarter resolution → bloom texture c) main pass: gate weave → softness → BLOOM / halation → grade (doc | light neutral B&W | film) → print + archive age → vignette → FILM GRAIN (in film coordinates, new every frame) → dust / scratches → flash. A_v15 diagnosis of the A_v14 grain (“a static grain image overlaid on top”). The A_v14 grain DID change every frame (an independent check measured ~0.035 correlation of neighbouring high-pass residuals); the sticker feeling came from its LOOK: • coarse 2.4 px value-noise clumps (blotchy), std 0.05, 60 % of it left in the deep shadows / highlights, + dust; • its clump layer was ONE noise field translated by ≈(32, 18) px per frame: after that shift consecutive frames correlate 0.52–0.54 (tools/grain_lab.py, GPU look-lab frames) → a pattern that slides over the picture; • grain was in SCREEN coordinates while the gate weave moved the picture under it → grain detached from the image. • a second, sine-hash 1 px grain (0.06–0.075) sat on EVERY shot incl. the speaker; sin() of large arguments loses precision on GPUs → patterned, and the grain changed character at every cut. • frame index was taken modulo 997 → the grain sequence repeated at 39.9 s. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Torn-paper COLLAGE motion film, 5–30 s (YouTube intro or channel trailer, brand or shop promo, 16:9), stop-motion on twos, built in code; AI only for photo cut-outs. Use for collage / scrapbook / cut-out / magazine-cutout / ripped-paper / mixed-media / zine-style videos, or when someone sends a paper-collage reference and says "make it like this ref" (RU: коллаж, рваная бумага, вырезки, аппликация, журнальные вырезки, заставка, интро, «сделай как на рефе», «как San Diego Zoo»). Not for static photo collages, moodboards, split-screen clip grids or a single transition. San Diego Zoo "Africa Rocks" technique: layered torn paper with white fibrous edges, halftone, watercolour sky, photo cut-outs dropping in, push into a lens → paper iris → kaleidoscope, strip rocket, title drop, page tear to the logo, logo flicker. Ships a working canvas engine, 10 s and 30 s example edits (kaye.creatives), a synthesised score with paper foley, palette remap, font and palette choice sheets, green-screen keying and render tools.

  • Struktur: 86 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: skrip top-level/entry point; tidak ditemukan deklarasi bernama oleh parser statis.
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: grade.js — palette remap as the very last pass of every frame (load after scenes.js, before film.js). Bake a palette into renders with window.PALETTE = '<name>' in index.html; preview others with ?pal=<name> (?pal=orig = original colours). roles of the original palette (collage.js C / collage_fx.js PAL + sampled scene colours) target palettes: only roles that change need listing (missing = keep)

  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # r5 San Diego Zoo "Africa Rocks" — frame analysis This is a 15-second torn-paper photo-collage animation. Real photo cut-outs (boombox, meerkats, a bateleur eagle, hyrax, klipspringer, acacias, B&W rocks) sit on hand-torn magazine paper with halftone dots and newsprint strips. Everything is animated on twos (12 drawings/s, every image held 2 frames, confirmed by frame differencing), so it reads as tactile stop-motion rather than smooth After Effects. There is no hard cut until the last second: the "camera" does one continuous trip. It pushes into the boombox speaker, goes through a 4-fold mirrored kaleidoscope tunnel, bursts through a torn hexagon hole into an eagle flight with a camera roll, rolls back to the meerkat savanna, and tilts up behind a meerkat that rockets on a plume of torn paper streamers. That tilt lands with an expo-out on a red/blue extruded title. The ending is a sticker-style page peel to a spray-paint wordmark on a torn strip, then a 0.58 s flicker through 8 alternate-universe logo styles. The energy comes from saturated cyan/red/mustard/chartreuse paper on white, white fibrous torn edges with soft drop shadows, replacement-animation pop-ups and constant scale changes. ## Shots - **0.00–0.42** [photo-collage] Establishing savanna collage, 16:9. Sky made of diagonal torn stripes: cyan paper with a halftone dot screen, a vermilion red stripe with white halft …

They are **building blocks, not a complete renderer or an existing project to run**. Create a new composition, source/asset manifest, transcript and timestamps, stage, media loader, masking system, frame capture, audio assembly, and encoder for each video. An implementation in another available renderer is acceptable if the visual result follows the skill. ## Included modules and dependencies Paths below are relative to this document. Keep the JavaScript files together so their relative imports resolve. | File | Purpose | Required support | | [engine.js](../implementation/browser-reference/engine.js) | Easing, absolute-time key sampling, crop geometry, selective `posterT()` | No imports; caller supplies current project dimensions and tracking | | [picture.js](../implementation/browser-reference/picture.js) | `Picture`: 2D composition input followed by WebGL grain/bloom/grade | Browser DOM, 2D canvas, functioning WebGL, decoded same-origin or CORS-safe media | | [split-layout.js](../implementation/browser-reference/split-layout.js) | Shared picture/type/effect-region geometry for presenter split entry | `engine.js`; caller implements drawing and clipping | | [typeLayers.js](../impleme …
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): | File | Purpose | Required support | | Version numbers in source comments are historical provenance, not target dimensions, scene IDs, validation rules or editorial instructions. The reference includes older optional looks and transitions; use only the modes permitted by the current skill. In particular, legacy neon, hard B&W, thermal, halftone, spring, bounce and flash options are not style defaults. | 1. Read the actual source metadata and requested delivery format. Set `width`, `height`, `fps` and duration from this project. Do not reuse an old timeline, crop track, media path, cache or audio mix. | 2. Create an explicitly sized stage and canvas. Override the historical `#stage { width: 1920px; height: 1440px; }` rule. CSS pixels must match master-frame pixels before any preview-only scaling. Size the output canvas before constructing `Picture`; its composition canvas and bloom buffers are allocated in the constructor and do not resize automatically. | 6. Update emphasis text with `type.update(t, split?.typeMotion ?? null)` and captions with `captions.update(t)`. These DOM layers are separate from the WebGL canvas. A canvas-only export will omit them. Capture the whole composed stage or composite text through an equivalent rendering path. | 7. For occluded text, use the actual layer order `background → text → exact foreground cutout`, with new tracked masks for the current source, crop and timestamp. The six included modules do not generate masks or provide a ready occlusion compositor. Text that must stay clean belongs above the grain pass; a foreground cutout used above it must match the underlying picture treatment.

Revisions must preserve successful and approved decisions; the absence of a technique that a scene does not need is not itself a defect. ## Preserve the foundation - Preserve the previous version; make changes in a new working version with clean layers. - Preserve the approved meaning, speech, scene order, duration, pacing, text and successful motion. If only the picture changes and the timeline is identical, retain the approved audio track without a new mix. - Treat inserts explicitly marked “keep” by the user in words or screenshots as approved. Match screenshots to the current timeline. Do not transfer lists of retained scenes from other projects. - Work with the original picture, text and treatment. Do not overlay a second set of captions or new grain on top of old versions already baked in. If necessary clean layers are unavailable, state exactly which asset is missing. - Record a short list of actual defects with current timecodes. Do not turn final refinement into an unjustified redesign of the entire video. ## 1. Cropping must not stretch people, objects or letters. - First build a timeline around meaning: thought → visual argument or association → readable emphasis → next thought. B-roll supports a specific line rather than filling random gaps. - Captions and emphasis words match the actual speech, names and numbers. Do not invent quotations, facts, product capabilities, interfaces or results. files/skill/kaye_creatives/My AI Workflow Skills/skill/Claude edit skill/implementation/browser-reference/picture.js · 21109 byte · .js

Fungsi / isi. Pipeline gambar reel: komposit kanvas lalu pass WebGL bloom, halation, grade, gate weave, grain, debu/goresan dan flash; frame ditentukan indeks waktu.

  • Struktur: 315 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: Picture.
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: A_v15 picture pipeline (A_v03 base, A_v14 film look, A_v15 rewrite of grain / bloom / B&W / archive age). 1. compose(): the shot runtime draws the current shot into a 2D "comp" canvas. 2. post(): WebGL passes over the comp. Everything is a pure function of the frame index — scrubbing is exact. a) bright-pass + 4× downsample b) separable Gaussian (H, V) at quarter resolution → bloom texture c) main pass: gate weave → softness → BLOOM / halation → grade (doc | light neutral B&W | film) → print + archive age → vignette → FILM GRAIN (in film coordinates, new every frame) → dust / scratches → flash. A_v15 diagnosis of the A_v14 grain (“a static grain image overlaid on top”). The A_v14 grain DID change every frame (an independent check measured ~0.035 correlation of neighbouring high-pass residuals); the sticker feeling came from its LOOK: • coarse 2.4 px value-noise clumps (blotchy), std 0.05, 60 % of it left in the deep shadows / highlights, + dust; • its clump layer was ONE noise field translated by ≈(32, 18) px per frame: after that shift consecutive frames correlate 0.52–0.54 (tools/grain_lab.py, GPU look-lab frames) → a pattern that slides over the picture; • grain was in SCREEN coordinates while the gate weave moved the picture under it → grain detached from the image. • a second, sine-hash 1 px grain (0.06–0.075) sat on EVERY shot incl. the speaker; sin() of large arguments loses precision on GPUs → patterned, and the grain changed character at every cut. • frame index was taken modulo 997 → the grain sequence repeated at 39.9 s. A_v15 grain: jittered-blob (sparse convolution) noise — Gaussian blobs at random points, one per cell, 3×3 neighbourhood, kernel tight enough …

Time-driven only — a pure function of programme time t. { id, style, text, t0, t1, x, y, size, align: 'left'|'center'|'right', color, w, enter: 'soft'|'blur'|'rise'|'cut'|'type'|'wipe'|'slam'|'pop'|'blurpop'|'draw'|'flicker', exit: 'cut'|'blur'|'fade'|'drift', exitDur (s, drift exit), caret, cps, words: [{w, t, it}] (per-word reveal on the spoken word), wordMotion: 'soft'|'rise'|'decel'|<blur default>, sub / qual / src (number style), A_v15: motion: { drift: [dx, dy] em/s, sway: em, swayHz, track: [from, to] em } — CONTINUOUS motion over the whole life of the layer, independent of the shot grid: a layer that spans a cut keeps moving through it (no reset at cuts). posterize: fps | {fps, from, to} | [{fps, from, to}, …] — stop-motion steps for THIS layer's animation only (absolute reel time); the picture and the grain keep running at 25 fps underneath. halo: true → soft readability halo instead of the hard drop shadow } The EDL may give meta.typeDefaults (merged under every layer) so the whole reel shares one motion language. `*word*` in text → italic serif accent. Fonts: three families only (src/fonts.js, css --f-sans / --f-serif / --f-mono). legacy (A_v03–A_v06), kept so older timelines still load

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Viktor Genboard Style — глобальный стандарт (движок + выдача) → Промпт-движок (жёсткая директива) → ЕДИНЫЙ БОРД (главное правило выдачи — жёсткая директива, нарушалось: не повторять) → Канонический движок борда (seedance-prompt-board / viktor-genboard-core) → Дизайн (обновление по прямому запросу Виктора 2026-10-10) → Журнал → Все генеративные чаты — прямой переход на общий Hub от 2026-10-10
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Viktor Genboard Style — глобальный стандарт (движок + выдача) Применяется во всех чатах, где генерируются промпты (видео и имидж) и строятся любые HTML-борды/артефакты/вьюеры. ## Промпт-движок (жёсткая директива) - **Все промпты во всех чатах пишутся ТОЛЬКО через скилл `ultralordgen-skill` (ULTRALORD).** Перед написанием камерной работы перечитывать его журнал — там живут актуальные каноны (DOYLE CAM v2 и новее). Законы ULTRALORD (ноль запретов в теле, закрытые инвентари, состояния-не-переходы, камера всегда в движении, пробелы вокруг @тегов, протокол эволюции) имеют приоритет над CINEDANCE и любыми другими промпт-скиллами. - Камерная работа: канон DOYLE CAM v2 (или новее из журнала): одна камера-мысль на кадр, камера-строка отдельно в конце сегмента, слои 近/中/远 + окклюдер, ширик пятью уликами + якорь 9.8mm, регистры А/Б, 反完美摄影锁, разрешённый камерный негатив-блок. **Ракурсы: избегать прямых фронтальных планов и играть углами — у каждого шота свой ракурс и высота камеры; тотальную диагональ/дач на все шоты НЕ навязывать.** - После подтверждённых фиксов — применять протокол эволюции ULTRALORD (лернинг в журнал, save_skill overwrite). ## ЕДИНЫЙ БОРД (главное правило выдачи — жёсткая директива, нарушалось: не повторять) - **Промпты НИКОГДА не выдаются одноразовыми jsx/HTML-вьюерами и не пересоздаются новым бордом в каждом чате.** Один борд живёт постоянным persisted-артефактом и …

Пропсы никогда не кладутся в персонажный борд и наоборот. Кнопка **Копировать** использует clipboard API и обязательный execCommand-fallback, копирует точный исходник и сообщает успех только после успешной операции; полный текст можно выделить, развернуть и скачать `.txt`. | - Правый клик по названию вкладки или сцены → инлайн-переименование (Enter/Esc, хранение в localStorage); у выбранной сцены есть видимая кнопка переименования. Сохранять прежние пользовательские названия и поддерживать стабильные ключи сцены вместо привязки только к меняющемуся порядковому номеру. | - **Порядок библиотеки:** каждая итерация несёт сквозной `seq`; история, сцены и вкладки сортируются по свежести, новый `seq` поднимает свою сцену и вкладку. Только выбранный текст создаётся полностью в рабочей области; библиотека и история показывают краткие строки, чтобы большие борды не строили все тела промптов одновременно. files/skill/kaye_creatives/My AI Workflow Skills/skill/JKD-FIGHT-ENGINE-2.12.0-2026-10-10-v2/skills/jkd-fight-scenes/SKILL.md · 29147 byte · .md

Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: JKD FIGHT ENGINE: исследовать экранные бои Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, JKD и выбранных соседних стилей; восстанавливать конкретные кинофрагменты и создавать связную хореографию. Вызывать при боевых сценах, приёмах, импактах, усилии тела и мимике обоих исполнителей. Использует исходные короткие коды S/F/H/K/T/G/W/D, WC и префиксы других стилей: BOX-H1, MT-K1, BJJ-G1, IA-W1; полный словарь находится в short-codes. Поддерживает рукопашные, клинковые, древковые, гибкие, метательные и огнестрельные постановочные профили с отдельными статусами источников. Сохраняет старые коды Виктора и S1 Warrior. Готовые промпты и аудит выполняет оригинальный ULTRALORDGEN с действующим генбордом.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): JKD FIGHT ENGINE v2.12.0 — современные бои, экранное исследование и восстановление кинофрагментов → Переносимый экспорт → Состояние проверки — 9 сентября 2026 → Приоритеты → Почти один в один: выбор режима → S1 Bai-jong — код Виктора, целевая манера Warrior → Художественный профиль Виктора → Ритм и продолжения → Экранное исследование и соседние стили → Теги вызова → Поимённый каталог всех запрошенных направлений → База и работа → Проверка → INGEST и сохранение
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # JKD FIGHT ENGINE v2.12.0 — современные бои, экранное исследование и восстановление кинофрагментов Скилл отвечает за содержание и пространственную связность постановочного боя. JKD даёт механику, художественный профиль Виктора задаёт манеру. Для готовых генерационных промтов применять действующие ULTRALORDGEN и viktor-genboard-style. Аудит и INGEST сами по себе не требуют генерации или доски. ## Переносимый экспорт Перед первым применением в новой среде прочитать [установку и границы источников](references/portable-installation.md). Перенос технических путей не подтверждает повторный просмотр или новую генерацию. ## Состояние проверки — 9 сентября 2026 Прочитаны прежние правила, 8 книжных конспектов и все 23 карточки присланных JKD-видео. Первичные книги и доступные новые транскрипты сверены в объёме, указанном в карточках. Это не полный повторный покадровый просмотр всех роликов и не проверка исправлений новой генерацией. Добавлены карта шести современных направлений, разбор речи двух спаррингов 2022/2026, WNG и Richardson, карта фильмов/сериалов и выборочные визуальные фазы источников, включая локальный Warrior. Точный охват — в карточках ниже. Библиотека расширяемая: это не «все существующие бои», не полный просмотр всех перечисленных фильмов и не доказательство совпадения генерации. Старый скилл смешивал несовместимые стойки и режимы ритма, терял условия книжных советов и …
