Then open After Effects, start Claude Code in any folder, and send: Use the voiceover-glass-reel skill. Here is my voiceover: /path/to/my_voiceover.wav Turn it into the finished reel: cut out all pauses and breaths, write the visual story from what I say, generate every picture in Higgsfield (a host lip-synced to my voice on an old TV, the characters, the locations, the story clips, the music), and build it in After Effects. Every generated clip goes in a floating rounded glass frame with a thin glowing border and a smooth push-in. When I list points, put a moving perspective grid behind them and flip each keyword's colour right as I say it. The main captions are big and spread across the frame, and the glass cards land exactly on the cut. Check it, fix what looks off, and render the final 1080p MP4. Optional additions to the same message: - `Script: <paste the text>`: names and spelling in the captions will then match the script. - `Make the host look like me: /path/to/my_photo.jpg` - `Look: colour, modern tech documentary`. The default is a black-and-white 1950s archival documentary. - `Accent colour: #FF3B30` Claude asks twice along the way:
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): 2. to approve the logo downloads (only names you actually say).

Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Turns ANY voiceover (and an optional script) into a finished 16:9 documentary-style reel in After Effects in one request: cuts pauses and breaths, writes the visual story, generates every picture in Higgsfield (characters, locations, story clips, a host lip-synced to the voice on an old TV, music), builds the edit natively in After Effects, renders a 1080p H.264 MP4. Look: dark archival documentary, clips in floating rounded glass frames with a glowing border, a moving perspective grid with keywords flipping colour, big captions, typewriter / giant-word / photo-card pages, flashes, synthesised SFX. Use whenever someone gives a voiceover, voice memo, narration or podcast clip and asks for a reel, video, short, explainer or edit made from it - 'make a video from my voiceover', 'turn this narration into a reel', 'glass frame edit', 'a clip from a voice-over', 'make a reel out of my voice recording', 'cut a video to my voice', 'glass frames and a grid' - even with no footage at all.

You do everything else and stop only: - **once** to get approval for the Higgsfield spend (give the total); - **once** for downloads such as logos. Work in the user's language in chat. Everything on screen is in the voiceover's language. ## What it makes Turns ANY voiceover (and an optional script) into a finished 16:9 documentary-style reel in After Effects with one request. It cuts the pauses and breaths, writes the visual story, generates every picture in Higgsfield (characters, locations, story clips, a host lip-synced to the voice on an old TV, music) and builds the edit natively in After Effects. Host portrait (1 image) → 2. TV plate (1 image) → 3. Character sheets (one per recurring character) → 4. Locations (3–6) → 5. Story clips (the bulk: ~1 clip per 3–5 shots) → 6. Host lip-sync clips (after `reel.py chunks`) → 7. Music (1 track) → 8. Logos (only for names that are spoken)
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Higgsfield generation: models, settings, prompts Everything visual is generated. Work through the Higgsfield tools: - `generate_image`, `generate_video` and `generate_audio`, or their `_batch` versions for several at once; - `media_upload` + `media_confirm` for local files (the faceboxed sheets and the host audio chunks); - `jobs_wait` until the jobs finish; - download the results into `<proj>/assets/`. Before you start: - check the balance; - add up the cost of the whole list and ask the user **once**; - make a project with folders 01 Characters / 02 Locations / 03 Video / 04 Audio when the tools support it. Test one item of each kind first (one sheet, one clip). Look at it, then batch the rest. ## Shared style line (put it at the start of every image and video prompt; adapt the era and place to the script) > Black-and-white 16mm archival documentary footage from a 1950s social-experiment film: heavy natural film grain, slight gate > weave, soft contrast, faint scratches and dust, real practical light, observational camera. For a modern or colour subject, swap in a matching documentary look. Keep it one look for the whole reel. People:

Soft diffused studio lighting, unretouched photography, sharp focus. Single subject only, exactly | > Realistic, grounded, no blood. Only these people. No text, no logos, no music. | - `generate_audio` must be true: `reel.py align` reads the clip's own sound to sync the lips. | ## 8. Logos (only for names that are spoken)

Fungsi / isi. Jembatan zsh untuk mengirim ExtendScript ke After Effects aktif dan menunggu hasil; lock/log dan kode keluar membedakan error, timeout, busy atau script tidak mulai.

  • Struktur: 79 baris; simbol yang dideklarasikan: __w.
  • Komentar pembuka / implementasi sumber: !/bin/zsh ae_run.sh <script.jsx> [timeoutSec=900] Sends one ExtendScript file to the running After Effects and waits for it. The only way this skill talks to AE. Inside the script use aeLog("text") to report (DoScript return values are useless). Printed here when AE finishes. Env: AE_APP (app name, default: newest "Adobe After Effects 20xx" in /Applications), AE_LOCK_ROOT (lock + logs). Exit: 0 ok · 3 script threw (ERROR line) · 4 AE still running it after the timeout (do NOT resend; wait, then check the log) 5 lock busy · 6 AE never started it (not running / modal dialog open) — safe to resend after fixing that. ---------- lock (one script at a time per Mac); a lock older than 30 min or of a dead process is taken over

The characters, the environments, the props, the voices, the visual language. Then every new episode is simply another story built on top of those same assets. That's exactly what you're going to build here, and it runs on one rule from start to finish: whatever you don't define, the AI will hallucinate. Everything in this pipeline exists to define things once and reuse them forever. Two tools cover the whole production: Higgsfield generates every image, video, and voice, and a Claude Skill turns your plain scene descriptions into complete production prompts. cartoon-scene-builder (1).skill SKIL Stage 1 — Art Direction Don't generate a single image yet. The mistake everyone makes is jumping straight into prompting — but every great animated show starts with art direction, because before you create a character you need the visual language of the entire series. Spend some time collecting references. Pinterest is great for this, and Instagram and ArtStation work too. Don't hunt for one perfect image — build a library of styles, colors, character designs, and environments that all fit the world you want to make. To save you a few hours, there's a ready-made reference c …

Generate multiple … | Create my main cartoon character from the attached photos, drawn in the exact art style of the attached style reference. Full body, neutral standing pose, clean plain background, front three-quarter view. This is the lead of an … | One great image isn't enough. The AI only knows your character from a single angle — ask for a different expression, pose, or camera angle, and it starts filling in the missing details on its own. That's where drift begins. | This is where the pipeline starts paying off. A new scene is now just your character sheet plus one location view — the AI already knows what both should look like; you're only telling it which character goes where. For a quick one-off cutaway you can skip the sheet and simply describe the environment, but for any location you'll revisit, a few extra minutes of views will save you hours. | Then treat voices exactly like visual assets: upload every one into your Assets with a clear name, so you always know which character it belongs to. Now your characters, locations, props, and voices are all saved — and every new scene is pulled together from assets instead of built from zero. | After hundreds of scenes, one lesson stands out: you almost never need to start over. If a shot isn't perfect, make the smallest change that could fix it — swap the key visual, rewrite a single action, regenerate one scene instead of the whole sequence. Because your characters, locations, and voices are locked, every iteration builds on the same foundation instead of rolling new dice.

SKILL.md

files/skill/sanjii/AI Cartoon - Full Breakdown/cartoon-scene-builder/SKILL.md · 14607 byte · .md

Fungsi / isi. Definisi skill/instruksi agen. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: Turns a simple scene idea into a production-ready animation prompt using your existing characters, locations, props, and voices. It automatically plans the shots, camera direction, actions, timestamps, dialogue, and references while keeping every scene consistent with the world you've already built. Use this skill whenever the user is making an AI cartoon, animated series, or animated short in Higgsfield with reusable assets (character sheets, location views, voice references) and describes what should happen in a scene or episode — phrasings like "make a scene where…", "next scene:", "build the prompt for this scene", "my character finds…", "new episode", "turn this into a production prompt". Also use it when the user wants to change a scene's length ("make it 5 seconds"), set up their show's world / Project Bible, split an episode into scenes, or fix a generation where a character drifted or voices got mixed up mid-scene.

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): Cartoon Scene Builder → Know the world first → Directing a scene → Output format → Worked example → Bigger than one scene → When a generation goes wrong
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Cartoon Scene Builder You are the director on the user's AI cartoon series. By the time this skill is in play, the world already exists: the user has built character sheets, location views, props, and voice references in Higgsfield. Your job is never to invent that world — it is to direct new scenes inside it. One plain sentence comes in ("Leo digs a mysterious remote out of the couch cushions"), one complete production prompt goes out: shots planned, seconds accounted for, camera called, actions blocked, dialogue timed, and every element bound to the right asset tag. The chain is always the same: **Idea → shots → timestamps → camera → actions → dialogue → references → final generation prompt** And the principle behind everything: **whatever the prompt leaves undefined, the model invents.** Undefined seconds become improvised action. Undefined speakers become swapped voices. Undefined framing becomes a random camera. A production prompt is good when it leaves nothing important to chance — while staying short and readable. ## Know the world first You can only keep scenes consistent with a world you can see. The world lives in the Project Bible: pasted text, an attached file (usually `project-bible.md`), or a filled-in copy sitting below the template in this skill. Asset tags given inline in a request ("i have @Rusty_Sheet, @Mia_Voice saved…") count too — never re-interview wha …

  • Struktur bagian (urutan sumber): @ricksclips3000 Short style → What's in the package → Setup → ffmpeg must be on PATH → optional: put Montserrat-ExtraBold.ttf (Google Fonts, OFL) in scripts/stage/fonts/ → Workflow → The four core rules → 1. Character → 2. Line → 3. Colour → 4. Camera → Supporting rules → Camera math → Scene JSON → QA checklist → Verified test (examples/test_render.mp4) → Limits
  • Cuplikan isi sumber: # @ricksclips3000 Short style Use this skill to plan, build, render or QA a vertical Short that looks and moves like the 20 most recent @ricksclips3000 Shorts. Every number here was measured frame by frame from those videos: 34,359 frames at 1080x1920 and 30 fps, condensed into 549 shot reference sheets. A number marked *observed* is a visual observation instead. `references/rules.json` holds every number in machine-readable form. ## What's in the package | Path | What it is | | --- | --- | | `SKILL.md` | This file: the rules, the camera math and how to run the stage | | `references/rules.json` | All measured numbers | | `scripts/stage/stage.js` | three.js stage: cutout characters, sun with shadows, tinted fill, measured camera glide | | `scripts/stage/index.html` | Page that loads the stage | | `scripts/stage/render.mjs` | Headless renderer: Chromium/WebGL to PNG frames to MP4 | | `scripts/stage/shortkit.py` | Assembler (dissolves, whips, captions, H.264) and rule checker; also animates plain stills | | `scripts/stage/package.json` | Node dependencies (three 0.170.0, playwright) | | `examples/example_scene.json` | Test scene with two placeholder characters | | `examples/test_render.mp4`, `test_render_frames.jpg` | The verified test render (also reproduced from a clean unzip + fresh install: 37.3 px/s, +6.01 %/s) |
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): # ffmpeg must be on PATH | If `npx playwright install` reports a read-only browser folder, set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` to a writable folder first. Headless Chromium renders WebGL2 in software (SwiftShader); `render.mjs` passes the flags. Expect about 0.45 s per 1080x1920 frame with 4096 px shadow maps on one CPU core. | Outline every drawn element with an even 10 px stroke (at 1080 wide) in plum-black, never pure black. | - Shadow hue: red-brown 40%, blue 32%, violet 25%. Neutral grey only 6%. Median shadow saturation 0.51. | - Always on screen; 1-2 words each. | - Farneback flow on 270x480 grey frames over an 8 px grid, keeping only textured points (gradient above 20).

About four words a second. 2. Ruang lingkup yang tertulis: The channel skill for @ricksclips3000-style animated Shorts - flat 2D doodle characters living in a sunlit 3D world, built entirely in code. Use it whenever the user wants to make, plan, render or check a vertical Short in this style, mentions "the channel skill", or asks for any step of it - generate the main character, an emotion sheet, slice a character into layers or rig a puppet, hand-painted textures, a 3D model of a prop, a background, the voiceover or music, "build the full 3D scene in code", a stop-frame check, a numbers comparison with a reference frame, or pastes a script and asks for the video. Generates every asset through the Higgsfield connector and assembles, checks and renders the video with the bundled three.js stage.

Body is a soft rounded bean-shaped torso covered by simple flat-colored clothing with one soft shadow tone; arms are thin solid black stick lines ending in small round black dot hands, hanging relaxed at the sides slightly away from the torso; legs are two thin solid black stick lines with no trousers, no feet and no shoes drawn, coming straight out of the bottom of the torso, slightly apart.   • Cuplikan isi sumber: # Measured style rules Every number here was measured frame by frame from the 20 most recent @ricksclips3000 Shorts: 34,359 frames at 1080x1920 and 30 fps, condensed into 549 shot reference sheets. A number marked *observed* is a visual observation instead. `rules.json` holds the same numbers in machine-readable form. Contents: the four core rules, supporting rules, camera math, QA checklist. ## The four core rules ### 1. Character Put one stick figure on screen whose round, outlined white head fills about a fifth of the frame width. - Characters are in 77% of shots. Of those shots, 57% have one character, 21% two, 11% three, 6% four and 4% a crowd. - Largest head: median 20% of frame width (~216 px at 1080); middle half 12-30%. - A round, outlined white or cream head in 94% of character shots. Thin stick limbs; costume and props carry the role (observed). - Method: a by-eye count of 61 sampled shots, good to about +/-5 points; automated head detection failed on this footage. - **Stage:** `"headWidth": 0.20` on a shot frames its target's head at 20% of the frame width. ### 2. Line Outline every drawn element with an even 10 px stroke (at 1080 wide) in plum-black, never pure black. - Width: median 10 px (0.9% of frame width); middle half 7-12 px; range 6-16 px. - Colour: median RGB 39/25/37 (#271925). Pure black appears in 2.8% of shots. - The 3D set carries no outline (observed …
  • Aturan/batas terpilih (kutipan sumber, bukan instruksi untuk pembaca): Outline every drawn element with an even 10 px stroke (at 1080 wide) in plum-black, never pure black. | - Shadow hue: red-brown 40%, blue 32%, violet 25%. Neutral grey only 6%. Median shadow saturation 0.51. | - Always on screen; 1-2 words each. | - The video length never changes with transitions, so the picture stays locked to the voice. | - Farneback flow on 270x480 grey frames over an 8 px grid, keeping only textured points (gradient above 20). | | Line | 10 px #271925 | 6-16 px, never pure black |

So, We Made 100 Videos.​ Iran launched another counterattack, and the Israeli military urged civilians to take cover, marking a two-year nightmare. I don't know what to say. Nas Daily is not a political channel, and I really feel like there's been a lot of suffering for everyone over the last two years. I don't know what videos we can make here because we're not CNN. So, here's what we decided to do: we're going to make 100 videos in 100 days starting tomorrow. Every video will be a lesson from the past, going back in history to see and learn from stories, even as far back as 1700 B.C., which we can now do thanks to A.I. For the next 100 days, we'll create a hundred lessons from history to make us wiser, more peaceful, more tolerant, and more compassionate people. By the end of these 100 days, I hope we have peace, and I hope you learn something from these videos. The beginning starts tomorrow. 2. Iran and Israel Used To Have Flights, Not Fights! Let me take you to the 1960s to show you Iran and Israel. Here, at the airport in Iran, flights went every day to Tel Aviv, not rockets, Boeing flights! Ladies and gentlemen, welcome aboard. Back then, 80,000 Jews lived in Iran, and they lived in peace right next to their Muslim neighbors. "Grab more Barbari bread! You'll need it to scoop up all those herbs!" Iranian students studied in Israeli universities. They spoke Hebrew, they debated politics, they made friends. The two countries even built an oil pipeline from the Persian Gulf to the Mediterranean! "Make sure the oil keeps flowing!" And yes, they even built weapons together. "Let's finish this before someone in Washington finds out." The people didn't hate each other. 20. Batas pemindaian & agenda verifikasi berikutnya

Yang belum dapat disebut telah dipahami penuh

  • Seluruh MP4: hanya byte/container dan durasi, belum ditonton frame-by-frame, belum ada transkrip atau pemetaan judul/scene.
  • Seluruh MP3/WAV: hanya metadata; identitas suara, bahasa, ujaran dan kesamaan waveform belum diverifikasi.
  • Guide Claude.pdf: 12 halaman citra; OCR dan peninjauan visual halaman belum dilakukan.
  • Citra di dalam paket skill: decoding/metadata, bukan penilaian subjek individual. Hanya delapan citra images/ dan styles/ ditinjau visual.
  • Font TTF dan model GLB: byte terinventarisasi; belum dirender/diinspeksi secara semantik.
  • Kode tidak dijalankan, dependensi tidak dipasang untuk render, aplikasi pihak ketiga/After Effects/macOS Vision tidak diuji. Referensi sumber web di dalam arsip tidak diakses ulang.

Pertanyaan untuk iterasi pengguna (bukan prasyarat audit ini)

  • Apakah prioritas berikutnya OCR Guide Claude.pdf, transkripsi VO, atau pemetaan video Nas ke naskah per shot?
  • Apakah duplikat paket perlu tetap diarsipkan atau kelak dikonsolidasikan? Tidak ada berkas sumber dipindah/dihapus pada tugas ini.
  • Versi ricksclips mana yang ingin dijadikan titik awal eksperimen? Keduanya tetap dipertahankan.
  • Apakah perlu manifest mesin-baca dan pengujian runtime per engine pada tugas terpisah? Output sekarang sengaja hanya dua file.
Tidak ada klaim bahwa template SaaS, koleksi prompt, seluruh video, atau aset lepas merupakan satu produk. Hubungan baru harus ditambahkan bersama bukti isi/path/timecode, bukan preferensi arsitektur.
